feature1.prompt: Return NotImplemented, not False, upon rich comparison with unknown type. Comparison methods should ideally return NotImplemented when unable to make sense of the arguments. This change ensures that when a custom class (for example, one implementing its own __eq__) interacts with a sympy object, the reflected method on the other object is called, resulting in a symmetric equivalence relation. If both sides return NotImplemented, the final result will correctly be False.
feature1.hint_texts: This part includes modifying the core library files to update the rich comparison methods (__eq__, __ne__, __lt__, __le__, __gt__, __ge__) so that they return NotImplemented in cases where the comparison cannot be performed. Implementers should locate patterns such as 'return False' and 'return not self.__eq__(other)' across the codebase and replace them appropriately. Changes should be applied consistently to adhere to Python's data model for comparisons.
feature1.entrypoint: Begin with sympy/core/basic.py (especially around line 316) and then update similar patterns in files like sympy/core/exprtools.py, sympy/core/numbers.py, sympy/geometry/entity.py, sympy/physics/optics/medium.py, sympy/physics/vector/dyadic.py, sympy/physics/vector/frame.py, sympy/physics/vector/vector.py, sympy/polys/agca/modules.py, sympy/polys/domains/domain.py, sympy/polys/domains/expressiondomain.py, sympy/polys/domains/pythonrational.py, sympy/polys/domains/quotientring.py, sympy/polys/fields.py, sympy/polys/monomials.py, sympy/polys/polyclasses.py, sympy/polys/polytools.py, sympy/polys/rings.py, sympy/polys/rootoftools.py, sympy/tensor/array/ndim_array.py, and sympy/utilities/enumerative.py. Look for any comparison methods that return False or use the negation of __eq__ and update them to conform with the NotImplemented behavior.

feature2.prompt: Ensure that rich comparison operations exhibit symmetric behavior when interacting with unknown types. By having comparison methods return NotImplemented, the reflected method from the other object will be invoked, ensuring that comparisons (such as equality and non-equality) yield the expected symmetric result. This update is essential for maintaining consistency when custom objects are compared with sympy objects.
feature2.hint_texts: This part focuses on updating and adding test cases to verify the new behavior for rich comparisons. Developers should add tests that create custom classes (e.g., Foo and Bar) to confirm that comparisons against sympy objects return NotImplemented when appropriate and that the symmetric property of these comparisons is maintained. The new tests should check both the cases where comparisons fail before the change and pass after, as well as ensure that existing valid comparisons continue to operate as expected.
feature2.entrypoint: Update the test files such as sympy/core/tests/test_basic.py and sympy/core/tests/test_numbers.py. Introduce new test cases that instantiate custom classes and validate that comparisons with sympy objects are handled as defined by the NotImplemented behavior. Use the modifications outlined in the test patch diff to guide the additions and changes to the test suite.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: The core library files (for example, sympy/core/basic.py and related comparison functions in various modules) and the test suites under sympy/core/tests are shared between the features.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Integrate Feature1's modifications to the rich comparison methods with the updated tests from Feature2. Both parts must pass continuous integration testing; Feature1 ensures the proper return of NotImplemented while Feature2 verifies the symmetry and behavior through dedicated tests both for cases that previously failed and regression tests that were previously passing.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 should coordinate with those responsible for Feature2 to ensure that the test cases accurately reflect the intended behavior of the modifications. Regular discussions and code reviews are needed to align on the expected delegation behavior and to handle any discrepancies discovered during integration testing.
